title: FilesWatchResult
description: Result of the files.watch JSON-RPC method: the refresh mode that now serves this binding's watch set. The call REPLACES the watch set rather than adding to it — the client sends the set it currently wants and the backend diffs, so collapsing a directory cannot leak a watch, and the swap is atomic and idempotent: a newly-added watch that fails to establish must not take the healthy existing watches down with it. The panel is told 'this directory changed' and never learns which mechanism said so; mode is the one exception, and it exists so the UI can say why refresh may lag.

mode.description: How the backend detects change for this binding. 'watching': live notifications (local fsnotify) are established. 'polling': the backend compares digest snapshots on a schedule — the designed mode for SFTP, which has no change notification, or a local fallback. The distinction between the first two levels is the whole point: designed-mode polling warns about nothing; degraded mode is a persistent badge.

degradedReason.description: Why refresh is degraded. Present only when a local watch could not be established and the backend fell back to polling — a plain string with omitempty semantics, never null — and the renderer shows the persistent 'Polling' warning badge beside Refresh only then, with this as the hover detail, clearing it the instant watching recovers. Absent for the designed modes: a remote binding is never degraded (polling is its designed mode) and a healthy local watch has nothing to explain.
